name: vpn
title: C. Relationship transport vs VPN
summary: A single VPN tunnel for all traffic. One operator learns a root-adjacent account (payment/login), the user's network location, every destination endpoint, and all timing. It moves the ISP's total view to one operator.

assumptions.join_kinds: ROOT_IDENTITY | RELATIONSHIP_IDENTITY | PAIRWISE_KEY | NETWORK_IDENTIFIER | SOURCE_ENDPOINT | DEST_ENDPOINT | TRANSACTION_ID | OBLIGATION_ID | CONTEXT_ID | RELATIONSHIP_LINK | ASSET | DENOMINATION | AMOUNT | TIME | CONTENT | CONTENT_SIZE | NETWORK_LOCATION | SESSION_IDENTIFIER

provenance: Authors' model of single-operator VPN disclosure (S11.C), 2026-09-03.
omitted: Jurisdiction and logging-policy claims of any specific provider.
Global passive observers (out of threat model, S0).
not_better_when: Arbitrary web browsing. Molt is for Pubky-native interactions; it is not a general VPN replacement.
joins_remaining_notes: Each relay sees the poller's network location; a TorTransport adapter (v2) can raise this boundary from Independent to CollusionBounded(1) under the declared assumptions.
Relays are chosen per (purpose, direction) so no relay sees more than one purpose of one relationship.
